prompt: In the core-infra channel, what is the workspace membership role of whoever reacted with a ✅ to the message about hitting the hard CUDA memory limit?
binding_note: Route: user_teams(r0).team_id = teams(r1).team_id; channels(r2).team_id = r1.team_id; messages(r3).channel_id = r2.channel_id; message_reactions(r4).message_id = r3.message_id; r4.user_id = users(r5).user_id (the reactor). The referent r0 is not just any membership in that workspace: the requested membership must belong to the same person as the reactor, so r0.user_id = r5.user_id is an explicit additional equality identifying which membership row is meant ('their own workspace role'). Because no message_reactions row has reaction_type = 'check' (or similar checkmark) on the target CUDA-memory-limit message, r5 is never populated, so r0 cannot be resolved.

obligations.name: reactor_membership
obligations.description: The user_teams row belonging to the same person as the ✅ reactor on the specific core-infra message about the hard CUDA memory limit (r0.user_id must equal the reactor's user_id, r5). No message_reactions row on that message carries a checkmark emoji, so no reactor exists and no membership can be resolved.
obligations.scope: workspace membership of the person who left a checkmark reaction on the identified core-infra message

task_spec.text: Find the message in core-infra about hitting the hard CUDA memory limit, identify who reacted to it with a ✅, and report that person's own workspace membership role.

access_plan: Use conversations.list to locate core-infra, then conversations.history/search.messages to find the message referencing the hard CUDA memory limit. Call reactions.get on that message's timestamp to enumerate its reactions and check for a checkmark-type entry (e.g. 'check'). If found, the reactor's own user_teams membership (their role in T01WORKSPACE) would be the answer via users.info's exposed workspace association. Since the seeded reactions on that message are only 'thumbsup' (Lukas) and the checkmark reaction that does exist ('check' by Priya) sits on a different message (the Tokyo latency-fix post), no reactor satisfies both conditions and no membership is discoverable.
